text:
Dana (PM): Quick shiproom — we need binding decisions for GA readiness. Focus: SLA targets, docs, oncall support, monitoring signals, and pricing must-haves.
Marco (Product Ops): +1. I put a light agenda in the doc: https://redwood-internal/shiproom/ga-bindings — please add blockers.
Priya (Support): Latest from support: we need runbook entries for 3 failure modes (model OOM, KV-cache corruption, degraded throughput). Otherwise T2 tickets will explode.
Leo (SRE): Agree. For monitoring we need: 99th pct latency SLI, token/sec per-host, and KV cache hit-rate. I propose alerts: latency > 500ms p99 for 10m, qps drop >30% for 5m, cache hit < 40% for 15m.
Ana (Pricing): Pricing note: Dedicated GA should have a standard reserved SKU + burst billing. We need unit cost targets: hosted gen <= $0.0009/token (90th), embeddings <= $0.0003/embedding. Are those acceptable?
Dana (PM): Those targets make sense as aspirational. We need to mark them as "GA targets" vs "contractual SLAs". SLA must be narrower: uptime, latency SLOs, and incident RTO/RPO.
Marco (Product Ops): Action: define which metrics are "contractual" vs "operational guidance". I can draft a table. Ownership? @Leo for telemetry, @Priya for runbooks, @Ana for pricing lines, @Dana for the final doc.
Priya (Support): Will write runbooks for the 3 failure modes. ETA EOD Tuesday. Will include playbook steps and communications templates.
Leo (SRE): I'll add dashboards and alert definitions to Grafana and Alertmanager. Will namespace alerts as rr-sla-ga-v1. ETA Wed noon. Also we need a canary rollout policy integrated in the console.
Dana (PM): Good. For SLA wording: uptime guarantee 99.9% monthly for hosted API; latency SLA: 99th <= 600ms for small models (seq<=512) — we should avoid committing to long-sequence targets until we have quant results.
Ana (Pricing): For packaging: free tier with soft QPS limits, pay-as-you-go, and 3 committed tiers for Dedicated. I'll prepare the rate card draft by Friday. Also flag: marketplace listing compliance requires privacy blurb.
Marco (Product Ops): Docs checklist: public API docs, changelog, upgrade guide, SLA T&Cs, incident playbook (internal), customer-facing runbooks (redacted). I'll create the checklist and link PRs.
DeployBot: Deploy note: staging->prod deployment scheduled 2026-04-01 02:00 UTC; canary window 30m. Auto-rollback on p99 latency spike >100% vs baseline.
Dana (PM): Key open decisions: 1) final p99 latency SLA number, 2) SLA credit policy (billing refund vs service credit), 3) oncall escalation path for Dedicated customers. Each needs an owner and due date.
Marco (Product Ops): I'll own SLA credit policy draft. Due Thu.
Priya (Support): I'll map escalation path and who to cc for Dedicated severity 1. Due Wed EOD.
Leo (SRE): I'll propose the p99 number after load tests finish Monday. Tentative: 550-650ms depending on model family.
Dana (PM): OK — owners and dates noted. If no blockers, we'll lock GA criteria in Thursday shiproom. Please update the doc and add "LGTM" once done. :thumbsup:
Priya (Support): Adding links to existing runbooks now.
Ana (Pricing): Adding draft rate card now.
Marco (Product Ops): I'll consolidate and post a summary before tomorrow's sync.
Dana (PM): Thanks — meet in tomorrow's 10am shiproom. If anything urgent, ping me.
DeployBot: NOTE: linked issue #4523 created for SLA T&Cs.
